description: Introduce the runtime regie controller (SceneRuntimeController) that coordinates cache/manifest + the EXISTING MediaSyncedTrackScheduler events + SceneRenderer. The controller is the single decision point for WHEN a scene is shown/hidden; it owns no clock, never commands the player, and is Android-independent as far as reasonable so it is JVM-testable via a thin renderer/preflight seam. Includes the regie unit tests (sections 9, 13, 14, 20-D, 21). Depends on FEAT-002 (bridge + atomic cache).
steps: Create SceneRuntimeController.java. It holds the active OverlayManifest (indexed by scene id, reuse the FEAT-002 index), the active revision, and a generation/revision guard counter. Expose a minimal seam interface for the actual drawing so JVM tests can run without Android: e.g. `interface SceneSink { boolean preflight(OverlayManifest.Scene scene); void show(OverlayManifest.Scene scene); void hide(OverlayManifest.Scene scene); void hideAll(); }`. In production the OverlayService adapter (FEAT-004) implements SceneSink by delegating to SceneRenderer; in tests a fake records calls.

Responsibilities (section 9): loadManifest(revision, manifest) / unload(); index scenes by id; onCommentDue(ScheduledTrack.Event) -> look up scene by event.id, if found call sink.preflight then sink.show, if not found do NOTHING (no render); onCommentExpired/onHide -> sink.hide; hideAll on eligibility loss; replaceRevision -> bump generation, unload old manifest, drop any visible scene from the old revision; never command the video player. The controller MUST NOT create a Handler/postDelayed clock for Video scenes — timing comes only from scheduler events forwarded in.

Add a generation/revision guard (section 14, 21): every onCommentDue is tagged with the revision/generation active when the scheduler produced it (or the controller checks the current generation at delivery). A late callback carrying an old generation must be ignored and must never resurrect an old scene. A double callback for the same scene must be idempotent (show once; second is a no-op or safe re-show of the same current scene, never a duplicate overlay). Deliver exactly one active visual scene at a time.

Exactly-one-visual-path contract (section 10, 30): the controller exposes/returns a deterministic signal that a valid manifest is active for the current revision (Case B). Define the authoritative predicate the OverlayService will use to pick Case A (legacy OverlayRenderer) vs Case B (regie+SceneRenderer) so the two never run for the same comment. Keep this as a pure method on the controller or a tiny helper (mirrors OverlayService.shouldShowOnEntry static-predicate style).

Eligibility (section 13): expose onEligibility(false) -> immediately hideAll (armed != visible) WITHOUT discarding the durable manifest/track or the loaded in-memory manifest; onEligibility(true) allows a subsequent due event to show again per existing policy. Do not alter MediaIdentityMatcher.

Pause/resume (section 12): the controller reacts to the scheduler's onPlayback(playing, pauseFreezesDisplay) only to the extent the legacy path already does (do not add a second clock). When pauseFreezesDisplay and paused, the visible scene must not be force-expired by wall time inside the controller; expiry/visibility continues to be driven by scheduler events. Keep this minimal and documented; do not reimplement the scheduler's freeze.

Add JVM tests for section 20-D (cases 16-22) and section 21: comment-1 due => scene comment-1 shown; unknown scene id => no render; a callback tagged with an old revision/generation => ignored (fake sink shows nothing new); replacing revision disarms the old scene (hide old, old-gen callbacks ignored); eligibility loss => hideAll called; pause/resume keeps the expected Video behavior (no second clock, scene not wall-expired on pause); exactly one renderer/scene active at a time. Section 21 async: render requested after a simulated stop/unload => ignored; double callback for same scene => idempotent (single show); a new revision received while a scene is visible => old scene hidden/disarmed and only new-revision scenes can show. Use a deterministic fake SceneSink and feed events directly; no Android, no real time.
acceptance_criteria: SceneRuntimeController is Android-independent (no android.* imports), owns no clock, never references TransportControls / media commands, and drives SceneRenderer only via the SceneSink seam.
onCommentDue shows the matching scene, shows nothing for an unknown id, and ignores callbacks from a superseded revision/generation (stale callbacks never resurrect an old scene).
Revision replacement disarms the old scene; eligibility loss hides immediately but keeps durable + in-memory manifest/track; exactly one visual scene is active at any time.
A deterministic predicate selects Case A vs Case B so legacy OverlayRenderer and SceneRenderer are never active simultaneously for the same comment.
Section 20-D (16-22) and section 21 async tests pass under :app:testDebugUnitTest.
findings: Added SceneRuntimeController.java (Android-independent, no android.* imports, owns no clock, never references transport controls). It holds the active OverlayManifest indexed by scene id (same by-id rule as VideoOverlayManifestBridge), the active revision, and a monotonic generation guard bumped on load/unload/replace. Drawing goes only through the nested SceneSink seam (preflight/show/hide/hideAll); the real SceneRenderer adapter is deferred to FEAT-004 as scoped. onCommentDue(event) and the generation-tagged onCommentDue(event, callbackGeneration) overload: look up scene by event.id, show when found+eligible+preflight-ok, do nothing for unknown id, ignore stale-generation callbacks, idempotent for the already-visible scene, exactly one visual scene at a time. unload()/replaceRevision() disarm any visible scene and bump the generation so late old-revision callbacks are ignored; durable cache is not touched. onEligibility(false) hides immediately (armed != visible) but keeps the in-memory manifest; onEligibility(true) allows a later due event to show. onPlayback records state only and performs no wall-clock expiry (no second clock; frozen scene stays visible on pause). Case A vs Case B selection exposed as the static predicate shouldUseSceneRenderer(manifestLoadedRevision, activeRevision) plus instance isSceneRendererActiveFor(activeRevision), mirroring OverlayService.shouldShowOnEntry style. Tests: SceneRuntimeControllerTest.java (14 tests) covers section 20-D cases 16-22 and section 21 async risks (render after unload/stop, double callback idempotency, new revision while scene visible, callback while ineligible, stale-generation ignore, preflight failure, expiry matching, null safety). Verification: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests => 13 OK; Gradle 8.9/JDK17 :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug => BUILD SUCCESSFUL; new test class reports tests=14 skipped=0 failures=0 errors=0. Did NOT modify OverlayService/SceneRenderer/CloudControlClient production wiring (FEAT-004) and kept all existing tests passing. Emulator-dependent api35 smoke and physical BRAVIA qualifications remain CI/human-only and were not claimed.
